bull_bear.body: Thin on this call — and the silence is itself the datapoint. An investor opened the door explicitly ("the healthy cash balance which is there on the balance sheet") and management answered only the capex half of the question, never the cash half. **No buyback, dividend or payout commentary at all this quarter**, versus Q4 FY26 where buyback was raised repeatedly and deferred in favour of growth. Net cash was >Rs.400cr at Q4 FY26 against FY27 capex of only ~Rs.100cr; nothing on this call narrows that gap or explains its use. The disclosed discipline is the 12–15% minimum IRR board gate and the capital-light structure of the renewable investment (26% equity, Rs.8.5cr, for 10.5 MW of capacity). Absent a deployment plan, the cash overhang carries into Q2 unaddressed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Anti-dumping FAILED — the single most important negative this quarter.** *"the Finance Ministry did not notify the anti-dumping duty, despite favorable findings by DGTR."* The Q4 thesis leg of a 10–30%-of-FOB pricing/sentiment uplift on NFY is gone for now. Chinese commodity filament yarn *"continued at very low prices."*
- **Margin reversion is guided, not speculative.** 15.46% → 7–10% band. The Rs.46.24cr inventory tailwind unwinds as higher-cost stock is consumed; caprolactam has already *"tapered down,"* which cuts both ways.
- **Caprolactam / nylon-chips volatility** tied to crude and geopolitics; management explicitly cannot forecast it.
- **Demand air-pocket risk after the GST-cut impulse.** Management's own list: *"evolving geopolitical developments, volatile crude oil prices and persistent inflation."* Their transmission mechanism is specific — RM-led price increases → *"deferment of purchases"* → lower new-vehicle demand and cuts across the auto value chain.
- **Import surge threat beyond China.** A newer framing than Q4: *"multiple countries having different geopolitical situations in their domestic markets, which could lead to surge in imports to the domestic markets." *Exports are minimal, so there is no offshore relief valve — the book is domestic and therefore fully exposed to import dumping.
- **Capacity ceiling.** 92 KTPA at 85–90% utilisation with zero FY27 addition. Volume upside is essentially capped this year; growth must come from realization/mix, which is exactly what management said.
- **Volume already rolled over QoQ.** 20,711 → 19,199 MT. Against Q4's stated aspiration to *"repeat our Q4-plus volumes"* in FY27, Q1 is a miss.
- **Renewable output is weather-dependent** — the ~50% share is a design forecast, not a contracted floor.
- **Fire/safety risk at old-layout plants** — remediation capex continuing post the Feb-25 Bharuch incident.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Consistent, disciplined, and — unusually — deflationary about their own record quarter. Sodani opened by pre-announcing the one-off (*"benefited from one-time inventory gains… we expect margins to normalize"*) before any analyst asked, which is the opposite of the usual pattern. Under sustained, well-argued pressure from Amit Kumar to concede a structural step-up to ~10% margins, he did not blink; he cut the questioner off (*"Have you completed?"*) and then gave a genuinely informative answer about *why* — the band will be revised only when it can be set at a level *"most likely not be breached, at least in normal circumstances, and definitely not on the lower side."* That is a company optimising for guidance credibility over near-term narrative.

Disclosure remains tightly rationed and the refusals are consistent quarter-to-quarter (single-segment reporting used to decline product capacity, value-added volume share, per-product margins, realization outlook, inventory-gain attribution). Two small tells: the CFO was almost absent from the Q&A (two short answers), and the call was closed with *"thank you everyone for joining our early call."* No hype language beyond the word "exceptional" in the prepared remarks, and even that was immediately qualified.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The refusal to raise guidance is the guidance.** Rs.86cr EBITDA less the Rs.46.24cr inventory line is ~Rs.40cr = ~7.2% margin — the *floor* of the 7–10% band. Management maintaining the band while printing 15.46% is not conservatism; it is arithmetic consistency, and it quietly validates using the full Rs.46.24cr as the haircut.
- **A record revenue quarter on falling volume.** Revenue +15% QoQ while volume fell 7.3% QoQ means realization rose ~24% sequentially. Investors modelling "record revenue" as demand strength will over-extrapolate; the correct read is that CENTENKA is a **spread business with an inventory-timing overlay**, and revenue is a poor proxy (the mirror image of FY26, when revenue fell 15% while PAT rose 52%).
- **Mix flipped to reinforcement inside one quarter.** NTCF went 52% → 57% of product revenue (+69% YoY vs NFY's +20%). Since NTCF is the high-barrier, non-commodity book and NFY carries the import-exposed commodity tail, the mix shift is *quality-positive* — and it partly explains margin without any one-off, a fact management never pointed out.
- **The anti-dumping failure changes the investment case's shape, not its size.** With no duty, the pricing uplift optionality is dead; what remains is the self-help route management has actually been executing — converting commodity NFY into customer-specific product that Chinese bulk supply structurally cannot serve. That is slower but is not policy-dependent. Watch whether they re-file or pursue the notification; the call gave no indication either way.
- **Capacity math caps FY27 upside.** 92 KTPA, 85–90% utilisation, zero FY27 addition, +3–4 KTPA only in FY28. Even a perfect demand year cannot deliver double-digit volume growth. Any FY27 revenue growth is price/mix, which reverses when caprolactam falls.
- **Renewable guidance was quietly restated upward twice.** Q4 said 36% → 48%; this call says >40% → ~50%, same commissioning window. Small, but it means the Phase-1 asset is running better than modelled — and it is the only lever on the call that is both structural and already partly delivered.
- **Watch the per-tonne power metric, not the power line.** Management pre-empted the Rs.190cr → −10% shortcut. The correct disclosure to demand next quarter is power cost per tonne, and they implicitly committed to it moving favourably.
- **Cash question dodged, buyback not raised.** After a quarter of Rs.62cr PAT on top of >Rs.400cr net cash and only ~Rs.100cr of capex, capital allocation went entirely undiscussed. That is a growing, unexplained overhang.

bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Nearly six decades of industry experience; the Directors presented the 60th Annual Report for FY 2025-26
- Stated leadership position in tyre reinforcement and synthetic yarns, backed by manufacturing excellence, deep customer relationships and commitment to quality
- Diversified product portfolio spanning nylon and polyester tyre cord fabric plus nylon filament yarn, which management says positions it to capitalise on long-term opportunities despite geopolitical and weather-related risks
- Value-added product (VAP) and customer-specific solutions strategy that reduces dependence on commoditised segments and supports sustainable margins
- Two integrated manufacturing sites (Pune and Bharuch) with dipping facilities at both plants
- Aditya Birla Group parentage and governance framework, including the Group's purpose and safety, sustainability and mental-health (MPOWER) programmes
- Captive renewable power access through an equity investment in ABREL Century Energy Limited; the Company achieved a 57% renewable power share and cites better availability of renewable energy as a support to performance
- Recognised operating standards - National Safety Award 2025 for Bharuch, CCI Water Excellence Award 2025 for Bharuch and the CII-ITC Award for Significant Achievement in Environment Management for Pune
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Low-priced imports and intense price competition from China and Vietnam in synthetic yarn — Persistent low-priced imports from China, surplus global capacity and a lack of robust trade protection measures are expected to maintain downward pressure on prices and margins; in the premium saree segment Nylon Filament Yarn also competes with Viscose Filament Yarn supported by low-cost Chinese imports. Mitigation is a shift to value-added products, differentiation and customer-specific solutions.
- Crude-linked raw material availability and cost volatility — Geopolitical tensions in West Asia had a significant impact on the availability and cost of crude-based raw materials; supply-chain disruption and higher input costs pressured the business, and global trade tensions produced a volatile raw material scenario.
- Export exposure to geopolitical uncertainty and global trade tensions — Exports as well as export-linked yarns were adversely impacted during FY26 because of geopolitical uncertainties, making a portion of the order profile dependent on factors outside management control.
- Weather and monsoon dependence of end demand — Management remains cautiously optimistic on FY 2026-27 despite below-normal monsoon forecasts; weather-related risks may moderately impact industry growth, and agricultural-equipment and agri-tyre demand is an important driver of Nylon Tyre Cord Fabric.
- Occupational health and safety — Identified as a material BRSR risk: even with proper training and well-established safety protocols, human errors can occur, potentially causing accidents, injuries and process failures; serious injuries can disrupt total man-hours and raise operational costs. Managed through HIRA, an ISO 45001:2018 certified system, Life Saving Rules, Process Safety Cardinal Rules and the MITR and MPOWER programmes.
- Water dependence and water-management risk — Dependence on water for manufacturing exposes the Company to water scarcity, supply disruptions and regulatory change; management also treats water as an efficiency opportunity, citing zero wastewater discharge, plants located outside water-stressed zones and 28 rainwater recharge wells at Bharuch.
- Waste management and environmental compliance — Poor waste-management practice can cause environmental pollution, legal violations and reputational harm; mitigated through source-level segregation, circular-economy practice, coprocessing of hazardous waste instead of landfill and disposal via authorised agencies under Central and State Pollution Control Board regulations.
- Legacy central excise litigation — A central excise matter over denial of the benefit under Notification No. 6/2000-CE remains unresolved: CESTAT upheld the denial and remanded for recomputation, the Company has appealed to the Supreme Court (matter tagged with similar appeals) and has sought a stay on recovery of interest and penalty, while the Department has challenged the Commissioner's revised order before the Appellate Tribunal. Management believes, on legal advice, that it has a reasonably strong case.

bull_bear.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)

business.body:
Single reporting segment — management repeatedly refused product-level breakups of capacity, value-added volume share and margins ("since we report our results in single segment, we will not be able to give the breakups"). What was given:
- **NTCF / reinforcement — Rs.306cr, +69% YoY, now 57% of product revenue.** The clear driver. Demand robust across two-/three-wheelers, tractors, PVs and heavy commercials, all "going quarter-on-quarter at a good pace." Management sees the GST-cut-led affordability shift as real but unquantifiable.
- **NFY / filament yarn — Rs.230cr, +20% YoY, flat QoQ.** Volume healthy with *"improving product mix, led by higher share of valuated and better margin products."* The commodity end of this book remains the exposed flank: *"import of commodity filament yarn from China continued at very low prices, while the Finance Ministry did not notify the anti-dumping duty, despite favorable findings by DGTR."*
- **PTCF / polyester industrial yarn** — still pre-commercial in tyre cord; the plant currently sells polyester industrial yarn, which management noted *"has an impact on our capacity"* utilisation optics while approvals run.
- **Group** — asked directly about Birla Cellulose: *"we do not have any transactions with them,"* but they co-develop products where nylon/polyester and cellulose overlap. No inter-company revenue to model.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Customer-specific product design as an import shield.** The clearest moat evidence on the call, and it is causal rather than asserted: Chinese supply is bulk/commodity, so any customer-specific spec must be converted domestically — *"if there any value addition is to be done to that, that has to be done by any competitor in the domestic market."* Against domestic competitors they claim *"a better edge in terms of quality, service, new product development."*
- **Stickiness translated into volume assurance, not just price.** Management explicitly linked value-addition to recurring offtake: *"more assured sales volume by targeting products to specific customers which get aligned with us and we get regular businesses from them over every quarter."*
- **Tyre-cord approval barrier.** PTCF requires a multi-stage, multi-year tyre-maker qualification (passenger-car safety protocols) — the same barrier that protects the incumbent NTCF book and is why the segment was never classed as commodity.
- **Structurally cheaper power via group captive.** >40% renewable today, ~50% guided, for only Rs.8.5cr of equity — a cost-position advantage bought with almost no balance sheet.
- **RM sourcing optionality.** Deliberately de-risked away from single-country dependence: *"to reduce the risk of having only dependence on China, we are already having other countries that we are sourcing from,"* plus domestic supply, with 25–30 days imported and ~15 days domestic inventory.

business.title: Quality certifications

latest_quarter.body:
Margin bridge for the quarter, in management's own ordering: (i) healthy volume growth YoY across all verticals, (ii) productivity improvements and higher operating rates, (iii) calibrated price pass-through of the raw-material increase, (iv) **one-time inventory gains from low-cost opening stock**, (v) higher renewable-power availability partially offsetting a rise in petroleum-based energy cost. Only (i)–(iii) and (v) are repeatable.

The mechanics management explained are worth holding onto: gross margin only moves on *sharp* RM moves — *"any small or more gradual volatility, whether going upwards or downwards, does not have a significant impact on margins. But a sharp increase or a sharp decrease in a very short period of a month or two months, that definitely has an impact."* The post-Iran-war caprolactam and chips spike was exactly that; those prices *"have a bit tapered down in this quarter and are volatile" —* i.e. the same mechanism that gave a Rs.46.24cr tailwind can hand back a headwind on the way down. Management would not size it: *"we do not give any forward-looking statements on what the impact would be."*

Power is the one genuinely structural lever: >40% renewable this quarter heading to ~50%. Asked whether the improvement is sustainable, Sodani said yes but honestly caveated it — *"it is definitely weather-dependent. It is not constant."* He then refused an analyst's attempt to convert it into a ~10% cut on the ~Rs.190cr FY26 power cost, insisting the correct metric is **power cost per tonne**, not the gross line, since the latter moves with volume, productivity and product mix.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Rev Rs.554cr (+38% YoY, +15% QoQ); EBITDA Rs.86cr, margin **15.46%** (+1050bps YoY, +400bps QoQ); PAT ~Rs.62cr (+301% YoY). Volume 19,199 MT (+12% YoY but **−7.3% QoQ**, below Q4's record 20,711 and below the "repeat Q4-plus volumes" aspiration). Mix flipped to reinforcement: NTCF Rs.306cr (+69% YoY, 57% of product revenue) vs NFY Rs.230cr (+20% YoY). **Inventory line-item Rs.46.24cr disclosed** — ex that, EBITDA ≈Rs.40cr / ~7.2%. **Margin band 7–10% REITERATED, explicitly not raised**, with a stated process for revising it later. **NFY anti-dumping FAILED — Finance Ministry did not notify despite favourable DGTR findings** (Q4's live thread now resolved negatively). PTCF on track: approval progressing with a few customers, commercial sales H2 FY27 (Q3 or Q4). Renewable >40% → ~50%, Bharuch 10–10.5 MW commissioning H2/Q3 FY27 (Rs.8.5cr equity, 26% group captive) — restated up from Q4's 36%→48%. FY27 capex >Rs.100cr reaffirmed; **no FY27 capacity addition**; mother-yarn project FY28 **+3,000–4,000 TPA (upgraded from +2–2.5 KT)**. IRR hurdle 12–15%. RM inventory 25–30 days imported / ~15 days domestic. **Capital allocation entirely undiscussed — no buyback/dividend commentary, cash question deflected.**
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did EBITDA margin land back inside 7–10% as guided, and how much of the Rs.46.24cr reversed; (2) volume vs 19,199 MT — does it recover toward 20.7 KT or confirm a capacity-capped plateau; (3) PTCF — any commercial sale booked, or does H2 slip to Q4/FY28; (4) Bharuch renewable — commissioned in Q3 as promised, and is renewable share tracking to ~50%; (5) any movement on the anti-dumping notification or a re-filing; (6) power cost **per tonne** disclosure; (7) does the cash pile finally get addressed (buyback/dividend/new segment); (8) NTCF vs NFY mix — does reinforcement hold 57%; (9) mother-yarn FY28 timeline and the 3–4 KTPA number; (10) whether the 7–10% band is formally revised upward._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** none given — standing policy of no forward-looking financial statements. Also declined on realizations ("changing on month-on-month basis… very difficult to even give a number").
- **Margin:** **7–10% normalized operating margin — REITERATED, not raised.** Pressed hard by two analysts to concede a step-up to ~10% given volume, mix and renewable tailwinds, Sodani held: *"we do maintain our last conversation on margins, which is that it would be between 7-10% on a normalized basis."* Separately committed to a *process*: *"once we are very sure that the range has improved, we will definitely revise and give that."* Direction for the rest of FY27 is **down from 15.46%** — *"we do expect the margins to normalize over the next few quarters."*
- **Volume:** explicitly **not** a growth lever this year — *"we are not adding any significant volumes in the current financial year in terms of capacity addition… the focus is more on the value addition and improving margins on the volumes that we sell."*
- **Order book / inflow target:** n/a (not an order-book business).
- **Capex / commissioning dates:**
  - **>Rs.100 cr capex in FY27** (reaffirmed from Q4).
  - **PTCF commercial sales commence H2 FY27** — *"hopefully, some commercial sales would start from Q3 or Q4. But H2, we definitely expect commercial sales to start."*
  - **Bharuch renewable expansion commissions H2 FY27, most likely Q3 FY27** — adds **10–10.5 MW** capacity; renewable share **>40% → ~50%**.
  - **New mother-yarn capacity commissions FY28**, adding **3,000–4,000 TPA** (upgraded from the +2–2.5 KT guided in Q4).
  - **New WAP investments during the year** for customer-specific value-added products.
- **Return hurdle:** *"we are looking forward for 12% to 15% minimum IR when we initiate the project"* — board-gated, and mgmt claims current projects clear it comfortably.

outlook.body: Not an order-book business; the forward proxy is (i) tyre/auto OEM offtake and (ii) the PTCF approval funnel. On demand, management said tyre-cord demand *"remained robust during the quarter following GST cuts on tyres and automobiles, with healthy growth across all automotive segments."* Notably they refused to attribute a number to the GST effect — the cuts landed *around September 2025*, so this is now the fourth quarter of a "continuing phenomenon" rather than a fresh impulse: *"how much is to be attributed to the GST cuts is a guess of anybody."* The PTCF funnel is the real pipeline item: approval *"is going on well with a few customers"* — no stage count given this quarter (Q4 had it at Stage 2 of 4).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **PTCF import substitution** — the single largest optionality. Domestic polyester tyre-cord market is ~25 KT and ~80–85% imported (per Q4 call); approval process *"moving in the desired direction,"* commercial sales H2 FY27. Goes into passenger-car tyres, so it rides PV growth rather than the plateauing truck/bus nylon pool.
- **Value-added / customer-specific portfolio ("valuated products")** — the stated strategic core. New **WAP investments planned during the year**. Management framed value-addition as serving two purposes, not one: better realization *and* volume defence — *"most of our value-added products are more customer specific and we reduce the import intensity or the competition by making products which are specific to the customer requirements. The products which come from China are more in bulk and are commodity products."* Value-added share is *"increasing year on year and it will continue to increase"* — but the actual percentage was refused.
- **Mother yarn capacity** — +3,000–4,000 TPA, FY28 commissioning. On a 92 KTPA base that is ~4% — this is a margin project wearing a capacity costume.
- **Renewable / power-cost structural reduction** — group-captive route, 26% equity contribution only. Phase-2 adds 10–10.5 MW, taking renewable share to ~50%.
- **Old-equipment efficiency capex** — a recurring, unglamorous lever: *"a lot of it will also be going on in reducing the power consumption, because particularly where the equipments have become old and inefficient."*

outlook.body:
- Broaden the customer base and expand geographic reach to offset a persistently challenging demand environment
- Increase the proportion of Value-Added Products (VAPs) in the portfolio to mitigate pricing pressure from imports and reduce dependence on commoditised segments
- Application-driven product development and customer-specific solutions to support sustainable margins in Nylon Filament Yarn
- Invest in Mother Yarn and DTY capacities, aligned with India's MMF-led textile transformation, to shift mix from low-margin commodity products towards higher-value apparel and technical textile segments
- Roll out additional production capacities, including the launch of Polyester Tyre Cord Fabric (PTCF) production, to diversify the sales portfolio in reinforcement fabrics
- Sustained cost optimisation and improvement of operational efficiency at manufacturing facilities
- Increase renewable energy consumption in the energy mix
- New Product Development and expansion of the premium product portfolio to sustain margins and performance
- Embed safety as a core operating pillar through Life Saving Rules, Process Safety Cardinal Rules, ISO 45001:2018 certified systems at both plants, and third-party HAZOP, fire and safety audits
- The routed governance text sets out capital-allocation intent qualitatively rather than as a dividend or balance-sheet policy. Growth is to be pursued organically: the strategic objective of maintaining the position as industry leader is to be met by increasing operational capacity through organic growth, making processes more efficient, focusing on technological advancement and better industry collaboration, with expansions undertaken according to customer requirements. A second strand is entry into new market segments and geographies, supported by investment in market research and analysis to identify product segments and diversification and by partnerships. Sustainability is treated as a capital-allocation priority in its own right through resource optimisation (water, waste and CO2 intensity reduction), policies and framework, and investment in human capital. Strategic planning is anchored in the Board's guidance and long-term business plan, cascaded across business units, with ERM, governance and controls as inputs. No dividend policy, buyback, debt-reduction or credit-rating intent is described in this section.
- Limited assurance on BRSR Core and non-Core indicators obtained from M/s BDO India Services Private Limited; BRSR reported on a standalone basis for Century Enka Limited
- Both Pune and Bharuch facilities operate under an ISO 45001:2018 certified Occupational Health and Safety Management System
- Zero wastewater discharge achieved from manufacturing operations, with plants situated outside water-stressed zones and water conservation measures to reduce overall consumption
- 28 rainwater recharge wells installed at the Bharuch site to support groundwater recharge, local water availability and groundwater quality
- Hazardous waste discharge reduced by installing a paddle dryer at the Pune facility
- Coprocessing of hazardous waste adopted as an alternative to landfill disposal, with source-level segregation and disposal via authorised agencies
- Green Polymer produced using process waste as a circular-economy initiative
- Reduce reliance on non-renewable energy and build sustainable long-term energy consumption goals; increased renewable energy consumption is a stated management commitment
- MITR (Making Individuals & Team Resilient) and MPOWER mental-health programmes run to support employee well-being, targeting zero injuries and no loss of manhours
- Bharuch facility honoured with the National Safety Award 2025 by the National Safety Council of India, and Gold Trophies from the Quality Circle Forum of India (Surat Chapter)
- Centralised grievance redressal mechanism with a dedicated email channel and defined escalation matrix covering communities, shareholders/investors, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company initiated steps to increase capacity of Draw Texturizing Yarn (DTY) and Mother Yarn, while continuing to focus on product customisation and the development of value-added products to expand its product portfolio. It also invested towards modernisation of plants and energy conservation measures during the period under review. Separately, the Company invested in ABREL Century Energy Limited in order to draw power from the second phase of that company's Hybrid (Solar and Wind) Power Project; the investment was made because a captive user must hold a minimum of twenty-six percent of the equity shares of the power producer to qualify as a Captive User under the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Electricity Rules, 2005. Going forward, the Company plans to undertake further capital expenditure towards modernisation initiatives, renewable energy generation, energy conservation measures, safety enhancements and infrastructure development, to improve operational efficiency and support sustainable growth. The routed text states no rupee capex budget, no commissioning dates and no capacity figures for these projects.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Reinforcement Fabric demand is projected to stay steady in FY 2026-27, supported by the replacement market, two- and three-wheelers, agricultural tyres and the expanding passenger vehicle segment
- Nylon Tyre Cord Fabric will mainly cater to the replacement market with consistent demand from two- and three-wheeler segments; Polyester Tyre Cord Fabric is set to benefit from ongoing growth in passenger vehicles
- Rising preference for radial tyres supports Polyester Tyre Cord Fabric demand, while commercial vehicle, agriculture, mining and construction demand underpins Nylon Tyre Cord Fabric
- The Indian Nylon Filament Yarn market is expected to grow at a medium-term rate of 6-7%, aided by the China+1 sourcing shift and rising demand for functional apparel, athleisure, sportswear, workwear and technical textiles
- Demand is particularly strong for Micro and Fine Denier Nylon Filament Yarns, with DTY products gaining increasing acceptance
- Government support for Make in India and man-made fibres, alongside water shortages and limited natural fibre production, is shifting the market towards nylon and other scalable synthetic options
- Margin headwind: persistent low-priced imports from China and Vietnam, surplus global capacity and lack of robust trade protection keep downward pressure on synthetic yarn prices and margins; NFY also competes with Viscose Filament Yarn in the premium saree segment
- Input cost driver: geopolitical tensions in West Asia affected availability and cost of crude-based raw materials, and global trade tensions produced a volatile raw material scenario
- Exports and export-linked yarns were adversely impacted during FY26 by geopolitical uncertainties
- The increase in automobile sales following the GST rate cut lifted demand for NTCF in the second half of the year
- Better availability of renewable energy, together with cost optimisation, supported overall performance
- Management is cautiously optimistic on FY 2026-27 despite below-normal monsoon forecasts, geopolitical uncertainty and volatile raw material prices

deepdive.thesis: The headline is a blowout — revenue Rs.554cr (+38% YoY), EBITDA Rs.86cr (+331% YoY), 15.46% margin (+1050bps YoY) — but it is almost entirely a *price and inventory-timing* quarter, not a volume quarter: sales volume actually fell 7% sequentially (19,199 MT vs 20,711 MT in Q4) while revenue per tonne jumped ~24% QoQ on caprolactam pass-through. Management disclosed a Rs.46.24cr inventory line-item in the reported results and reiterated — twice, unprompted, and again under direct questioning — that the *normalized* operating-margin band remains **7–10%**, explicitly refusing to raise it. Strip the inventory number at face value and EBITDA is ~Rs.40cr / ~7.2% — the floor of that band, which is why the refusal to upgrade guidance is the most honest signal on the call. The two live structural threads moved in opposite directions: the NFY anti-dumping duty **failed** (Finance Ministry did not notify despite a favourable DGTR ruling) while PTCF commercialisation stayed on track for H2 FY27.

Margins to normalize DOWN from 15.46% as higher-cost inventory replaces low-cost opening stock (directional only - management refused to quantify)
Will formally revise the 7-10% band upward only once confident the new floor will not be breached - a checkable promise to re-guide

Total FY27 capex spend (reaffirmed from Q4 FY26 guidance)
Bharuch renewable power expansion to commission in H2 FY27, most likely Q3 FY27 (same window guided in Q4 FY26 - slippage watch)
Normalized operating margin band maintained at 7-10%; explicitly REFUSED to raise it despite printing 15.46% this quarter
Renewable generation capacity to be added at Bharuch under the group-captive scheme
No significant capacity addition in FY27 - growth to come from value-addition and margin, not volume
New WAP investments during FY27 to expand the customer-specific valuated product portfolio (amount not quantified)
Equity already contributed to the 26% group-captive renewable JV dedicated to Century Enka
Second hybrid/renewable project (~similar to Phase-1 ~16 MW installed) expected to start in H2FY27, most likely Q3, with company equity contribution under Rs. 10 crores.
